authorityBoundary: These are source-scope candidate assignments. familyIds is the union of separately identified role assignments, not a mandatory all-worker bundle. conditionalTriggers are not assigned until their actual exposure is confirmed. Source references support scope and qualification research; they do not mandate VNDRLY family codes. Existing 59 knowledge/program courses do not supply licensed, clinical, trade or specialist operational qualification.
sourceReview: Individually classified all 321 service names and source categories using explicit row groups, not regex assignment. All matching crosswalk original labels/categories/locators are retained; original Achilles page-76 extraction and BPCL text checked for ambiguous scope. Specialist official sources consulted separately. No claim that every source PDF page or an actual contract/job was reviewed.

conditionalTriggers: Actual field visit or operational-site work by otherwise desk-only personnel — A source engineering/consultancy title does not itself make the worker an operator.
Driving, delivery, trailer use or loading is actually performed — No driver course is assigned merely because an office adviser supports a transport client.

Applicable commercial/regulated driver qualification is established for the actual vehicle, cargo, route and jurisdiction — License class, endorsements and carrier obligations require a competent applicability decision.
New or unfamiliar task or changed role — Task familiarity rather than calendar tenure determines support needs.
Worker supplies equipment operation, lifting operation, rigging or signaling — Rental without an operator and desk engineering do not include these duties automatically.

Worker issues permits, isolates, tests atmosphere or performs designated electrical control functions — One endorsement does not imply the others; practical scope and employer/site authority remain separate.
Worker is assigned first aid or specialist response/rescue duties — Awareness training and a response plan do not confer practical responder competence.
Actual work at height, scaffold use or access/fall equipment duties — Ground-level construction does not automatically involve a fall exposure; actual access method determines assignment.
Actual welding, flame cutting, grinding or other hot-work method — Cold forming and desk fabrication engineering do not automatically include hot work.

Actual entry into a classified permit-required or otherwise controlled space; respiratory use requires separate exposure-based determination — A tank, vessel or cleaning label does not itself prove entry. Atmosphere, respiratory use and rescue requirements require actual assessment.
